title: Mighty, while hiding (Judges 6:11–16)
hookLine: the angel calls a frightened man threshing in secret "thou mighty man of valor"

cards: A man is threshing wheat in a winepress. Threshing is open-air work: you beat the grain on a flat floor and let the breeze carry the chaff away.
Gideon is down in a pit for crushing grapes, out of sight, hiding the wheat from the Midianites, who have raided the harvests until Israel is left with nothing.
He's crouched in a hole, beating a little wheat by hand, listening for riders. And under the oak nearby, an angel of the Lord sits watching him. His first words don't fit the scene at all.

teach.h: THE GREETING: MIGHTY MAN OF VALOR.
teach.b: The angel says: "The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour." Mighty. To a man in a hole.
He asks a hard question: if the Lord is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are the wonders our fathers told us about, the ones from Egypt? It's a complaint.
Some rabbinic readers also hear a man speaking up for his people, and say that's part of why he was chosen. Then the Lord tells him: go in this might of yours, and save Israel. Which might?
So far Gideon has hidden wheat and asked why.

teach.h: POOREST FAMILY, LEAST IN THE HOUSE.
teach.b: He says so himself: my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. The answer isn't a speech about hidden talents.

teach.h: THE ANSWER: I WILL BE WITH YOU.
teach.b: It's this: I will be with you. The strength comes with the promise. And the angel never scolds the fear, or the question.
He doesn't wait for Gideon to stop being scared.
He calls him mighty while he's still hiding, and lets the name go ahead of him, the way a coat is held out before someone has stood up to put it on.

how: Jews study the Gideon chapters as part of the Former Prophets, and rabbinic commentary often asks why a frightened man threshing in hiding was the one chosen.

o: a title Gideon earned after winning his first battle
what the angel called Gideon while he was still hiding
what his family called him as their eldest son

games.q: mighty, while hiding — tap the pairs.
p: if God is with us, why all this?

s: the angel called Gideon mighty after he won a battle

if the Lord is with us, why has all this happened to us?

games.q: you're hiding wheat in a winepress, listening for raiders. a stranger under the oak says: the Lord is with you, mighty man of valor. what do you say?
o: thank him and get back to work.
ask why, if God is with us, all this has happened to us.
games.why: Gideon asks the hard question: where are the wonders our fathers told us about? the answer doesn't scold him. it says: I will be with you.

practice: Let one frightened person you know come to mind, and look for what they're already doing while they're scared: getting up, showing up, keeping someone fed. Name it, silently, as strength.
If you pray, hold the angel's first words over them: the Lord is with thee.

wordCard.voice: Mighty. What the angel calls Gideon while he's hiding wheat in a winepress, before he has done one brave thing.

orig.note: Hebrew: mighty man of valor, the angel's name for Gideon in Judges 6:12.

carryVoice: Your line: a coat held out first. The name came before the courage. Day seven hundred seventeen.
